title: ArrayList versus LinkedList
context: How do ArrayList and LinkedList differ, and which should you use?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: ArrayList is backed by an array. It has O(1) random access and good cache locality, and it is the default choice. LinkedList is a doubly linked list. It has O(1) inserts and removes at the ends and when you already hold the node, but O(n) access by index, and each node uses more memory. Benchmarks usually favour ArrayList, even for many middle inserts. Use LinkedList mainly as a Deque, and prefer ArrayDeque when you only need a queue or stack.

points.title: Default is ArrayList
points.why: Random access and cache locality usually win in real code.

points.title: Prefer ArrayDeque for queues
points.why: ArrayDeque is faster than LinkedList for stack and queue use.
